A Newar artist and architect from the Kathmandu valley in Nepal, born in 1245, who rose to lead the imperial workshops of the Yuan dynasty in China. He died in Beijing in 1306.

In 1260 he went to Tibet as the young leader of a team of Nepali craftsmen, sent to build a golden stupa for the Tibetan lama Phagpa, who was Kublai Khan's teacher. Phagpa took him on to the Mongol court. There he won Kublai Khan's favour by repairing a bronze figure that Chinese craftsmen could not fix.

His best known work is the White Stupa of the Miaoying Temple in Beijing, finished in 1279, a tall whitewashed stupa in Nepali and Tibetan Buddhist style that still stands. He also made statues, portraits of the imperial family, and led the bureau of artisans. Through him and his pupils, Newar art shaped Buddhist sculpture and painting across Tibet and Yuan China. In Nepal he is a national hero, and a highway out of Kathmandu bears his name.
sum: A Newar artist and architect from the Kathmandu valley in Nepal, born in 1245, who rose to lead the imperial workshops of the Yuan dynasty in China. He died in Beijing in 1306.
